subject: Physics
description: Discovery, types of decay, carbon dating, half-life problems, applications

options.option_text: Marie Curie, who later isolated radium
Henri Becquerel, while studying uranium salts
Ernest Rutherford, who studied alpha decay
Albert Einstein, who explained mass-energy

questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel — Paris, 1896. Found that uranium salts emitted rays that fogged photographic plates, even in the dark, without external excitation. MARIE + PIERRE CURIE later (1898) isolated polonium + radium, coined 'radioactivity'. RUTHERFORD distinguished alpha + beta + gamma rays (1899-1903). All four (Becquerel + Curies + Rutherford) won Nobel Prizes; Marie Curie won twice (Physics 1903, Chemistry 1911).

questions.stem: Three types of radioactive emission have characteristic CHARGES:

options.option_text: All three carry positive charge equally
Alpha +2, Beta −1, Gamma uncharged (zero)
Alpha −2, Beta +1, Gamma carries positive charge
All three are completely uncharged in nature

questions.explanation: Charges: ALPHA = +2 (helium nucleus, 2 protons + 2 neutrons); BETA-MINUS = −1 (electron); GAMMA = 0 (photon, electromagnetic radiation). Penetrating power inversely related to mass + charge: α (stopped by paper) < β (Al foil) < γ (lead/concrete). Ionising power opposite: α > β > γ. Identifying via deflection in magnetic field: α and β deflect oppositely; γ doesn't deflect.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 dating is used to estimate the age of organic remains. Its half-life is approximately:

options.option_text: 100 years, useful for medieval dating
5,730 years, useful up to ~50,000 years old
1 million years, useful for fossil dating
4.5 billion years, the age of the Earth

questions.explanation: Carbon-14 (¹⁴C) — radioactive isotope of carbon. Half-life ~5,730 years. Continuously formed in upper atmosphere (cosmic rays + N-14); incorporated into living organisms. After death, no new ¹⁴C taken in; existing ¹⁴C decays. Measure ¹⁴C/¹²C ratio → estimate time since death. RANGE: ~50,000 years (after that, too little ¹⁴C left to measure). For older artefacts: K-Ar (potassium-argon) for million-year scale; U-Pb for billions of years (rocks, Earth's age). Distractor 4 = U-238 half-life (4.47 billion yrs).

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits an ALPHA particle, its mass number decreases by 4 and atomic number by:

options.option_text: 1 unit (one proton lost from nucleus)
2 units (two protons lost from nucleus)
0 units (no proton change in alpha)
4 units (matches mass number drop)

questions.explanation: Alpha particle = ⁴₂He (2 protons + 2 neutrons). Emission reduces mass number by 4, atomic number by 2. Example: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + α. Element changes (uranium → thorium). Beta-minus emission: atomic number INCREASES by 1 (neutron → proton + electron + antineutrino), mass number unchanged. Beta-plus / positron emission: atomic number DECREASES by 1. Gamma emission: no change in either.

questions.stem: If 16 g of a radioactive substance is left after 4 half-lives, the original amount was:

options.option_text: 64 g, four times the remaining mass
256 g, sixteen times the remaining mass
32 g, two times the remaining mass
128 g, eight times the remaining mass

questions.explanation: After n half-lives, remaining = original × (1/2)ⁿ. 4 half-lives → remaining = 1/16 of original. 16 g = original/16 → original = 256 g. Verify: 256 → 128 (1 HL) → 64 (2) → 32 (3) → 16 (4). Distractor 1 = 64 g would be after 2 HL. Distractor 3 = 32 g after 1 HL. Distractor 4 = 128 g is 1 HL stop short.

questions.stem: Cobalt-60, used in cancer radiotherapy, primarily emits which type of radiation for treatment?

options.option_text: Alpha particles, for surface tumours only
Gamma rays, with high penetrating power
Beta particles, suitable for skin cancers
Neutrons, for boron neutron capture therapy

questions.explanation: Cobalt-60 (Co-60) — emits BETA particles + GAMMA rays. The high-energy GAMMA rays (1.17 + 1.33 MeV) are used in EXTERNAL BEAM RADIOTHERAPY for cancer (high penetration → reach deep tumours). Half-life 5.27 years. Also used in food irradiation (sterilisation), industrial radiography, sterilising medical equipment. Distractor 1 — alpha can't penetrate skin; not used externally. Distractor 3 — beta in some skin therapies but not main Co-60 use. Distractor 4 — different therapy (BNCT, uses boron + thermal neutrons).

questions.stem: The SI unit of radioactivity (decays per second) is the:

options.option_text: Curie (Ci), an older unit of activity
Becquerel (Bq), one decay per second
Sievert (Sv), a unit of dose equivalent
Gray (Gy), a unit of absorbed dose

questions.explanation: BECQUEREL (Bq) — SI unit of radioactivity = 1 disintegration per second. Named after Henri Becquerel. Older non-SI unit: CURIE (Ci) = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq (activity of 1 g of radium-226). SIEVERT (Sv) — biological dose equivalent (effective biological damage). GRAY (Gy) — absorbed dose (energy/kg deposited in tissue). Annual safe limit for general public: ~1 mSv (excluding natural background ~2.4 mSv).
